entries.name: GENET
entries.definition: A connectionist architecture for finite constraint satisfaction that represents variable assignments by active label nodes and alternates input-maximizing assignment updates with increased inhibitory weights on violated constraints when the network stabilizes without a solution.
entries.identity_notes: This is the GENET constraint-satisfaction architecture described by Davenport, Tsang, Wang and Zhu, including the general-constraint extension. It is not a biological genetic network, genetic algorithm, trained classifier or synonym of GLS. The binary network has inhibitory nogood connections, while the general-constraint extension includes constraint nodes and asymmetric fixed/adaptive connections. A Hopfield identity or globally symmetric network mapping would overstate that general architecture. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 307 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 4 and 4 lines respectively. All eight text hits were prior discovery leads in the two checkouts, not existing candidate records. Eight exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and five native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The source explicitly says GENET is not complete: learning may create other local minima. It supplies no guarantee of finding a satisfying assignment or proving unsatisfiability within a finite budget.

Exactly synchronous updates can oscillate; the source footnote excludes that interpretation of the parallel pseudocode. Ties can change assignments without strict objective improvement, distinguishing this mechanism from the strict hill-climbing record.

The 1994 experiments use a sequential C++ simulation. Proposed speedups from future VLSI implementations are expectations, not measured hardware results curated here. The GENET2 conflicted-variable variant is not silently treated as the default variable-selection rule.

General-constraint output functions and representations require care. At an atmost bound, activation in the same variable cluster must account for all participating values; independently inhibiting each inactive value can introduce a false penalty. No numerical benchmark result is curated.

claims.statement: Create one cluster for each finite-domain variable and one label node per possible value, with exactly one active label per cluster. In the binary formulation, incompatible label pairs have inhibitory connections initially weighted −1; a label input sums the weights from currently active connected labels. A cluster activates a label of maximal input, breaking ties randomly. These updates need not be strict improvements. The described parallel implementation is explicitly not exactly synchronous, and the reported simulator selects variables sequentially. When an update cycle leaves the assignment unchanged, terminate if all active-label inputs are zero; otherwise reinforce violated connections, using W_new=W−V_i*V_j in the binary case. The extension represents higher-order constraints by constraint nodes with fixed label-to-constraint inputs and adaptive inhibitory outputs to labels. For a violated general constraint, all its outgoing connection weights are decremented according to Equation5; this must not be silently replaced by the binary active-endpoint rule. The paper defines distinct output functions for forbidden tuples and atmost constraints.

entries.name: Extended Guided Local Search
entries.definition: The Tsang–Mills–Ford extension of Guided Local Search that combines cost-scaled penalty weighting, aspiration for a new best original-objective solution despite an augmented-objective penalty, and probabilistic random neighborhood moves.
entries.identity_notes: EGLS here denotes the combined coefficient, aspiration and randomness extension in CSM371. GLS+A and GLS+R are separate ablations, not exact aliases of the combined algorithm. The method modifies the GLS search framework; it is not FLS activation-bit bookkeeping, simulated annealing, or a generic name for any later GLS extension. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 307 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 4 and 4 lines respectively. All eight text hits were prior discovery leads in the two checkouts, not existing candidate records. Eight exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and five native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The report title does not establish a parameter-free algorithm. Feature definitions, neighborhood and local solver, cost estimate C, coefficient a, randomization probability P_r, initialization and stopping remain choices; the proposed defaults were evaluated only in the reported problem settings.

The literal aspiration inequality is strict in both original improvement and augmented deterioration. It does not specify equality handling when h(s_next)=h(s_current); the underlying local solver and concrete implementation must declare that boundary and the order of random versus ordinary/aspiration moves.
Scaling by a typical cost contribution is problem-dependent. The TSP first-tour average is not a universal normalization for arbitrary objectives, especially zero, negative or mixed-scale terms.

Random moves can worsen either objective and need not improve exploration on a particular step. Aspiration protects access to an examined new original best, not global optimality or monotonic improvement of the entire trajectory. No comparative performance claim is curated.

claims.statement: Retain GLS feature counters, augmented objective h=g+lambda*sum(p_i*I_i), and penalty increments for present features tied for maximal cost/(1+p_i) utility. Scale lambda=a*C, where C estimates a characteristic cost contribution; the TSP illustration uses the first local-minimum tour cost divided by the number of cities. Add the report’s literal aspiration condition: accept an examined neighbor with g(s_next)<g(best_so_far) even when h(s_next)>h(s_current). This bypasses an augmented-cost rejection; it does not erase feature counters. Add randomization so that, with configured probability P_r per move, a randomly selected neighbor is accepted regardless of its objective or penalty quality. The combined EGLS uses all three changes. Its reported recommendations a=1 and P_r=.2 are experimental defaults, not universal constants or a proof of parameter independence.

entries.name: Guided Genetic Algorithm
entries.definition: The Lau–Tsang genetic-search framework that uses shared adaptive solution-feature penalties both to modify fitness and to construct per-chromosome gene weights that bias crossover and mutation.
entries.identity_notes: This record identifies the named Lau–Tsang GLS/genetic hybrid, not every algorithm described informally as guided genetic search. Later template-guided, fuzzy-guided or distributed algorithms are not asserted equivalent from their names. Generic GA supplies population evolution and GLS supplies feature penalties; GGA adds penalty-derived per-gene templates and specialized variation. It does not replace the population by the probability vector used in PBIL. LPGA is a problem-specific precursor, not an exact alias. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 307 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 4 and 4 lines respectively. All eight text hits were prior discovery leads in the two checkouts, not existing candidate records. Eight exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and five native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The source initializes counters and template weights to zero but its displayed crossover and roulette rules divide by total weight or draw from an empty integer range when that total is zero. Neither inspected method supplies the fallback. A uniform fallback or pseudocount is an implementation decision requiring separate evidence; none is asserted here.

The displayed mutation comparisons maximize g, whereas the article identifies the illustrated application as minimizing augmented cost and explicitly notes descent in footnote4. The record preserves this inconsistency and states objective-best selection with an explicit minimizing convention, rather than claiming the printed pseudocode is directly executable unchanged.

The stagnation trigger is a heuristic, not a certificate that every possible improving gene change or population transition has been exhausted. The thesis’s future-work discussion states this limitation. Penalty updates need not escape all local traps or reach a global optimum.

The application’s elitist replacement, finite mutation count, tie multiplicity and zero-weight handling do not define a unique universal implementation. Feature encoding, scaling and penalty semantics affect results; the reported benchmark superiority is not curated as a general guarantee.

claims.statement: Maintain a population and a shared set of nonnegative feature-penalty counters, initially zero. Define each feature by an exhibited variable assignment or group of assignments and an application-specific undesirability cost. When the best current population member’s fitness remains unchanged for a configured number of generations, increment all maximal-utility present-feature counters, with utility cost/(1+counter). Use the augmented objective f+lambda*sum(counter*indicator) for the minimizing formulation and recompute each chromosome’s template: a gene weight sums counters for its exhibited features that involve that gene. Thus weights depend on the chromosome under shared penalties; offspring templates are recalculated, not inherited. At a crossover position with positive total parental weight, choose parent1’s value with probability weight2/(weight1+weight2), favoring the lighter gene. For mutation with positive total template weight, sample a gene in proportion to its weight and choose an objective-best domain value, with random tie handling in the displayed operator. The manuscript decrements a changed gene’s weight only if positive and allows repeated gene selection. Population replacement, mutation/crossover rates, stagnation threshold and stopping are configurable; the application uses elitist parent-plus-offspring replacement. These statements describe the documented framework and positive-weight operators, not a complete executable specification for all boundaries.
